newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Africa's Alliance Air mulls adding second plane.
newsitem.headline: Africa's Alliance Air mulls adding second plane.

text.p: Alliance Air, a regional airline jointly owned by South Africa, Tanzania and Uganda, is looking to add a second aircraft to meet the demands of its expanded flight plans, its chairman said on Tuesday.

"We are starting a new route, Kilimanjaro to London, in August. We are thinking of starting the Gulf route -- Dar es Salaam, Dubai, Bombay. We will be needing a new aircraft," Alliance Chairman Joseph Mungai told Reuters.
Mungai said the airline, which began flying in 1995 with one leased aircraft, was considering adding an Airbus aircraft to complement its less fuel-efficient 19-year-old Boeing 747SP.
"Fuel performance, that is largely what will really dictate it. Ge'll go for the kind of aircraft that is a good performer," he said.
Mungai declined to speculate on which Airbus model Alliance might use.
He added the airline, which flies twice a week to London and between Dar es Salaam, Entebbe and Johannesburg, was happy with its current investment in the Boeing 747.
"The lease rate that we are getting is excellent."
Mungai said Alliance partners Air Tanzania and Uganda Airlines, which own 30 percent each, continued to examine a possible merger with the airline.
"Integration is a real prospect," he said.
South African Airways holds the remaining 40 percent of Alliance.
Mungai said Alliance had recently forged links with private operators Air Rwanda, Aero Zambia and Zambia Express.
Alliance planned to synchronise its flight schedule with Air Rwanda and use the link with the Zambian airlines to access Zambia's capital, Lusaka.
